tasks.notes: Duplicated event-log readers: `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` exports `RUN_DIR_PATH`, `ENGINE_EVENT_ID`, `ENGINE_EVENT_LINE`, `B32`, `runDir`, `eventsRaw`, `evidenceEventsRaw`, `eventsFile`, `evidenceEventsFile`, `events`, `evidenceEvents`, `publishEvents`, `eventsOfKind` and `ulidTs` (the Context asks for exactly this, so the siblings can read the same record), but `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs` imports none of them and re-implements every one locally: `HOME_TARGET_RUN`/`runDirOf`/`runEventsPath` restate `RUN_DIR_PATH`+`runDir`, `evidenceEventsPath` restates `evidenceEventsFile`, `eventsAt`/`events`/`evidenceEvents`/`isPublish`/`publishOf`/`ofKind` restate `events`/`evidenceEvents`/`publishEvents`/`eventsOfKind`, and `B32`/`tsOfId`/`ENGINE_EVENT` restate `B32`/`ulidTs`/`ENGINE_EVENT_LINE`. The result is two sources of truth for the rig's run-dir path and for the engine stub's line, one of which (the helpers') has no call site anywhere in the tree and so is exercised by nothing. Fix inside this task's FILES: import `runDir`, `eventsFile`, `evidenceEventsFile`, `events`, `evidenceEvents`, `publishEvents`, `eventsOfKind`, `ulidTs` and `ENGINE_EVENT_LINE` from `./_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` and delete the local copies, deriving the leg's `ENGINE_EVENT` from `JSON.parse(ENGINE_EVENT_LINE)` so the stub line is pinned in one place. Nothing a criterion depends on is at risk today — the exam is green — so this is advisory.; Silent type fallback in `append_event`'s writer (`fleet/sandbox-boot.sh`): the `i` tag does `try: event[name] = int(value) / except ValueError: event[name] = value`, so a `number` that is not an integer is recorded as a JSON string instead of failing or logging. The contract sentence this task adds and M1 both fix `number` as the answer's integer, and the surrounding code otherwise has explicit error paths (the `case "$out"` arm that logs `event: could not append`). Suggest logging the coercion failure through the same `log` path rather than substituting a string cell. The green case is covered by leg (a), so this is defensive-path only.; Duplicated reader logic: `fleet/tests/_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` gains thirteen new exports for reading the event log — `RUN_DIR_PATH`, `B32`, `ENGINE_EVENT_ID`, `runDir`, `eventsRaw`, `evidenceEventsRaw`, `eventsFile`, `evidenceEventsFile`, `events`, `evidenceEvents`, `publishEvents`, `eventsOfKind`, `ulidTs` — and nothing in the tree imports any of them (only `ENGINE_EVENT_LINE` is used, inside the stub script). `fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs` instead re-implements every one of them locally: `HOME_TARGET_RUN`/`runDirOf` re-spells the run-dir path the helper's `RUN_DIR_PATH`/`runDir` already spells, `evidenceEventsPath` re-spells `evidenceEventsFile`, `eventLines`/`eventsAt`/`events`/`evidenceEvents` re-spell `eventsRaw`+`events`/`evidenceEvents`, `isPublish`/`publishOf`/`publishIn` re-spell `publishEvents`, `ofKind` re-spells `eventsOfKind`, and `B32`/`tsOfId` re-spell `B32`/`ulidTs`. The task's Context asks for these readers in the helpers "so the sibling sims can read the same record"; as written there are two copies that can drift, and the shared one is dead code in a file a concurrent run is also editing. Fix: import `runDir`, `eventsFile`, `evidenceEventsFile`, `events`, `evidenceEvents`, `publishEvents`, `eventsOfKind`, `ulidTs`, `B32` from `./_sandbox_boot_helpers.mjs` and delete the local re-definitions, keeping only the sim-specific `unstamped`, `ID_RE` and the one-JSON-object-per-line assertion (which is worth folding into the helper's `events`). No exam leg changes behaviour.; M4/leg (h) requires "the file's first line is byte-identical to the line the engine left", and Global Constraint 1 requires that no line the engine wrote is changed. The submission checks this as `assert.deepEqual(all[0], ENGINE_EVENT)` (fleet/tests/test_sandbox_boot_selfmerge.mjs, leg (h)) — a comparison of the *parsed* object, which would still pass if the boot rewrote that line with different bytes (reordered keys, different spacing, `ensure_ascii` differences). The helpers already export `ENGINE_EVENT_LINE` for exactly this check and it is unused. The implementation itself is correct (`open(path, "a")` only appends), so no criterion is actually false; the exam clause is just verified in a weaker form than it names.
